open_obligations: Note that the capability gap is information access, which Khan et al. list as a limitation.
Check whether ground truth is used only for evaluation, as sandwiching requires.
Note that no model is aligned in an inner loop.
in.other_title: Human judges 88% with debate vs 78% consultancy; LLM judges 76% vs 54% (naive 60% / 48%)
in.rationale: Bowman et al. ask whether debate can be validated empirically under sandwiching. Khan et al. report non-expert human judges reach 88% with LLM debate versus 60% naive and 78% consultancy, with GPT-4-Turbo debaters who can read the story; the experts are LLMs with privileged information rather than more capable models, and no fine-tuning is done by the non-experts.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate between LLMs helps non-expert judges beyond a baseline, in a hidden-passage QuALITY HARD setup

open_obligations: Note the unequal number of turns between debate (3) and market-making (1).
Note that the supervisor is a model, not a non-expert human as in sandwiching.
Check that the four tasks have a strong-weak gap large enough for a sandwiching analogy.
in.other_title: Debate beats consultancy and market-making as the source of weak-model context
in.rationale: Bowman et al. ask for empirical trials of debate and market-making. Lang, Huang and Li report that replacing debate with market-making or consultancy as context for training the weak model gives lower test accuracy and PGR on all four tasks; the 'weak supervisor' is a 7B model trained on transcripts, not a human, and market-making and consultancy run for one turn while debate runs for three.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate and market-making differ as sources of information for a weak supervisor, for Qwen-14B agents and Qwen-7B weak models on NLP classification

open_obligations: Check whether the setup counts as sandwiching given that experts are humans, not a model more capable than the non-experts.
Note that no model is trained or aligned in the inner loop.
Check how ground-truth labels are used for evaluation versus Bowman et al.'s expert outer loop.
in.other_title: Debate beats consultancy for non-expert human judges: 84% vs 74% on hard QuALITY questions
in.rationale: Bowman et al. call for empirical trials of debate under sandwiching. Michael et al. have non-expert judges who cannot read the passage judge debates between experts who can, reporting 84% for debate versus 74% for consultancy; the 'model' is often a human expert and there is no fine-tuning loop, so it is a relaxed sandwiching test.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate helps non-experts supervise better-informed experts, in a sandwiching-like setup on QuALITY-hard
